title: Human Things by Joshua Owen starring Victoria Clark #humanthingsplay ...
transcript: A human skewer, a climate disaster, and a giant golden egg are all on the menu in this bizarre and allegorical play starring Tony-winner Victoria Clark. On a remote island, a young couple is studying declining bird populations when another couple stumbles in from a shipwreck. Oh, and there's a huge storm coming. Unfortunately, this premise sounds a lot more interesting than how it's executed. Act one is primarily exposition, and its grounded tone ends up being a red herring. Act two is where it gets interesting and more surreal. The plot is pretty shaky though, as is some of the acting — not Victoria Clark's. She is the primary selling point and the symbol of the play’s themes, an assignment she excels in quite easily. Despite the compelling threads this play has to offer, they don't coalesce with this story and set of characters. The thesis, so to speak, feels both nonspecific and heavy-handed. It's hard to effectively unpack the meaning of life, motherhood, and lifetime companionship in a two-hour play — mind you, this is Joshua Owen's first play. Maybe we would have gotten closer to the crux of at least one “human thing” had the play been more focused and either less outlandish, or significantly more. With that, another program for my collection.
